acceptance_criteria: Start with no completed cycle reports starting, never current.
A normal cycle advances sequence, completion time, fully observed time, and aggregate coverage counts.
A synthetic in-flight cycle spanning multiple intervals increments skipped-overlap evidence and transitions to late or stalled at declared boundaries.
A single unavailable marker, log, or typing source reports partial coverage without suppressing healthy peers.
Repeated identical source failures form one bounded episode with counts rather than one log per tick.
Recovery is emitted once after a fresh successful observation and preserves generation continuity.
Stop reports stopped, clears timers, and cannot later emit a completion from an obsolete generation.
Restart changes generation and requires post-restart observation proof.
Wall-clock rollback or advance cannot create false freshness or recovery.
Health, WebSocket hello, and console transport or data-state projections consume the same cycle snapshot.
Mutation tests fail if skipped ticks, bare catches, or partial coverage are projected as fully current.
Public telemetry and tests contain only aggregate or reserved synthetic values and no locations, identities, payloads, credentials, process data, or raw exception text.
blast_radius: Fleet realtime invalidation lifecycle; message, access, log, feed, and typing source observations; timer overlap and shutdown behavior; aggregate health and metrics; WebSocket producer-state projection; console current, partial, late, stalled, and failed states; incident and recovery correlation; and public observability documentation.
evidence_summary: Two identical live GraphQL reads established issue #2522's node identity, title, URL, open state, empty label set, update time, and exact 10,091-byte body hash. The API body already ended in one newline, and its SHA-256 was computed directly over the returned string without adding a synthetic newline. The exact SSH remote main and local tracking ref both remained at pinned revision a91f5301266fae2049cd1ae1b3c1b236a7ea2aa8, and the decisive poller blob matched that revision byte-for-byte. Thirteen deterministic pinned-source assertions confirmed that the poller stores only a timer, last-good marker and typing maps, and a private overlap latch; overlapping calls return without a receipt; per-instance database failures, absent typing ports, non-200 typing responses, and typing exceptions do not produce coverage state; stop clears internal state; sixteen lifecycle and coverage tokens are absent; and the only source-tree consumers construct, return, start, and stop the poller. Four focused write-free suites passed 48/48 tests. They prove current diff emission, duplicate-timer containment, in-flight overlap suppression, log rotation, typing last-good preservation, publisher behavior, and WebSocket behavior, but expose no cycle-health snapshot or skipped-overlap counter. A fully paginated all-state scan covered 518 issues in six pages and 1,984 pull requests in twenty pages. Closed #1087 with merged PR #1333 added the correct overlap guard; closed-unmerged PR #1628 was superseded by merged PR #1643's behavioral coverage; merged PRs #1334/#1353 and #2423 preserve narrower log and typing correctness. The current open-PR scan covered all 39 pull requests, 43 changed-file pages including every continuation page, and 1,333 changed files. It found no direct or closing #2522 reference, no open implementation owner, no open change to the poller, publisher, WebSocket server, or focused tests, sixteen shared-document collisions, and one meaningful taxonomy coordination point in PR #2451. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The issue would be falsified by one bounded, externally consumable poller snapshot that distinguishes starting, current, partial, late, stalled, failed, and stopped; advances generation and sequence; records monotonic duration and lag; counts scheduled, completed, skipped, and failed work; declares expected, observed, and unavailable sources; preserves last-good comparison state; and requires a fresh fully observed post-restart cycle before recovery. Exact pinned-source assertions found none of those properties. This lane did not add the audit-only failing tests needed to inject a never-resolving cycle, partial source failures, clock movement, stop during flight, or restart generation because mutation was restricted to this review record. The 48 passing tests therefore prove stable existing behavior, not cycle freshness or coverage. No production runtime probe was attempted, so observed operational incidence and alert thresholds remain measurement obligations rather than verified outage claims.
impact: A live timer and quiet log can look healthy while realtime invalidation cycles are skipped, stalled, partially observed, or repeatedly failing. Operators and downstream clients cannot distinguish a current producer from stale last-good state, cannot measure how much fleet coverage is missing, and cannot prove recovery after restart. That can leave browser caches and aggregate fleet status stale while transport reachability still appears green.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read the live issue identity, title, exact body hash, labels, update time, exact SSH remote main, and every open pull-request body, head, closing-reference page, and changed-file page immediately before registry integration or metadata mutation.

Sequence typed database-marker observation outcomes from #2520 before declaring marker coverage complete, while keeping #2522's aggregate cycle lifecycle separate from #2520's domain-event correctness review.
Coordinate the stable lifecycle and observation vocabulary with #2447 and current PR #2451, but do not let taxonomy documentation substitute for executable producer-state evidence.

Require RED and GREEN tests for starting without completion, a fully observed cycle, one unavailable source, a never-resolving cycle across multiple scheduled ticks, repeated identical failures, recovery, stop during flight, restart generation, and wall-clock movement.

Verify duration and freshness decisions use monotonic time, wall-clock fields are display-only, counters and ages are bounded, and high-cardinality source detail stays behind an authorized diagnostic projection.
Verify one unavailable marker, log, or typing source preserves last-good comparison state while marking aggregate coverage partial and allowing healthy peers to complete.

Require the health, metrics, WebSocket hello, and console reconciliation projections to consume one versioned snapshot and prove that timer existence, process reachability, an open socket, or a log line cannot mark the producer current.

Keep automatic restart out of the initial visibility change; review any later self-heal policy separately for explicit authority, event-loop and planned-shutdown classification, rate and flap bounds, generation change, and post-restart fully observed recovery proof.
Re-run focused tests plus mutation tests at the exact candidate revision, and treat any skipped, masked, flaky, or resource-rejected probe as inconclusive rather than green.

Use reserved synthetic values in every lifecycle, source, event, metric, log, and UI fixture; publish no live identity, payload, path, location, credential, raw exception, process detail, or topology value.

suggested_remediation: Add a versioned read-only snapshot to the realtime poller with generation, lifecycle, monotonic sequence and lag, wall-clock correlation times, bounded scheduled/completed/skipped/failure counters, and expected/observed/unavailable source counts. Make every scheduled source end in a typed observed or unavailable outcome, preserve last-good comparison state across partial cycles, project one aggregate snapshot through health, metrics, WebSocket hello, and console reconciliation, and emit bounded failure and recovery episodes. Establish this visibility before considering a separately reviewed, explicitly authorized, rate-limited self-heal policy.
